sections.content: How many people stayed in South Shields after gaining qualifications?

South Shields is a large town in the North East. South Shields does not have its own university.

South Shields has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, South Shields ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,665 state-school pupils from South Shields who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 910 (25%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,225 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare South Shields to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of South Shields' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in South Shields in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left South Shields move to?

Of South Shields's graduates, 235 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those graduates (34%) were living fairly locally, in the Newcastle travel to work area (TTWA).

Of South Shields's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 215 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 120 of those qualified non-graduates (56%) were living fairly locally, in the Newcastle travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in South Shields' GCSE cohort:

  • 130 graduates left the North East
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber
  • 70 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 18% of graduates and 18% of qualified non-graduates living in South Shields had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 800 graduates and 1,190 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in South Shields. This is compared with the 910 graduates and 1,225 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 82% of the graduates had also lived in South Shields as GCSE pupils, while 18% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in South Shields in 2018 to 2019, 83% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 18% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
